title: Minimum Number of Operations to Sort a Binary Tree by Level
summary: Given a binary tree with unique values, determine the minimum number of operations required to sort the values at each level in a strictly increasing order by swapping values between nodes at the same level.
statement: Given a binary tree with unique values, determine the minimum number of operations required to sort the values at each level in a strictly increasing order by swapping values between nodes at the same level.
constraints: The nonempty binary tree has unique values.
One operation swaps any two values on the same level.
Return the minimum total swaps that make every level strictly increasing.

hints: Each level is an independent permutation-sorting problem.
Traverse by BFS, map each unique value to its sorted position, and count permutation-cycle swaps.
For each position, repeatedly swap its mapped destination into place and add one.
A permutation cycle of length c needs exactly c-1 arbitrary swaps; summing those minima across independent levels yields the global minimum.
